new_source_delta.mechanism: The 14500-character regulator now progressively compresses profile, halves then removes hyperposition, removes the possibility-space, and only then emits a stderr warning if world/frame still exceed the budget.

primary_sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
primary_sources.finding: Long-context performance depends strongly on the position of relevant information, so total length alone is not a sufficient semantic preservation metric.

primary_sources.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
primary_sources.finding: Faithful prompt compression requires preserving essential information and evaluating downstream behavior; naive token removal is not an adequate guarantee.

primary_sources.title: Retaining Key Information under High Compression Ratios: Query-Guided Compressor for LLMs
primary_sources.finding: Compression can collapse toward closed-book performance when key information is removed; relevance-aware retention is a necessary control.

hypotheses.claim: The ordered five-stage shedding policy stays within budget while preserving task-relevant evidence better than size-matched random deletion or oldest-first truncation.
hypotheses.test: On frozen exact source/tree and held-out queries, log component characters and hashes before/after each stage; compare current policy, random deletion and oldest-first truncation at identical final size. Score answer correctness, evidence recall, epistemic residual value and latency.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current shedding loses more required evidence or yields worse held-out outcomes than either control, or component totals do not reconcile to final context.

hypotheses.claim: Hyperposition and possibility-space are genuinely lower-value, reconstructible signals whose removal does not damage decisions under load.
hypotheses.test: Create paired cases where required evidence exists only in hyperposition or possibility-space, then force stages 4 and 5 while holding all other context fixed.
hypotheses.falsifier: A correct decision becomes incorrect or ungrounded specifically after either signal is dropped.

hypotheses.claim: No over-budget context may proceed as an ordinary turn; overflow becomes a typed, receipt-bound nonmeasurement.
hypotheses.test: Inject an irreducible world/frame larger than 14500 characters. Require status OVERFLOW_ERROR, zero downstream model call and a conserved component trace in the atomic run receipt.
hypotheses.falsifier: The current warning-only path still calls the model or any consumer renders the turn as measured/successful.

counterhypotheses.attack: Equal length does not imply equal relevance or positional accessibility; current source has no semantic preservation test.
The deletion order is architectural judgment, not an empirically bound value ranking.
The function returns the oversized context after warning, so execution can continue unless a downstream caller independently rejects it.

new_concepts.name: Semantic Shedding Ladder
new_concepts.definition: A declared priority order for removing context components under pressure, each rung carrying an independently tested information-loss budget.

new_concepts.name: Budget Compliance Without Fidelity
new_concepts.definition: A context satisfies its size limit while silently losing the information required for the task.

new_concepts.name: Warning-Only Overflow
new_concepts.definition: An invariant violation is logged but the invalid object is still returned into normal execution.

new_concepts.name: Context Conservation Trace
new_concepts.definition: A receipt that reconciles component sizes, hashes, removal stage and retained evidence to the exact final prompt.
